chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The deliberate act is everything whereby one intends something and strikes it with an iron implement, or with a stone, or with a stick, or with a punch — all of this is deliberate. And the erroneous act is when one intends something but strikes something else.

key_terms.الْخَطَأُ: Error/mistake — the legal category where harm occurs unintentionally (target missed), resulting in liability for diya (blood money) rather than qisas
key_terms.الْعَمْدُ: Deliberate/intentional act — the legal category where the perpetrator targets a specific victim, resulting in liability for qisas (retaliatory punishment)
key_terms.بِوَكْزَةٍ: A punch or forceful thrust — included to indicate that bodily harm need not involve a weapon to be classified as deliberate

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between deliberate (amd) and erroneous (khata') killing in Shia Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the legal distinction between deliberate (amd) and erroneous (khata') acts of bodily harm or killing. The deliberate act is characterized by targeting a specific person or object and striking them with any instrument — whether iron, stone, stick, or bare hand. The erroneous act occurs when one aims at one target but accidentally hits another. This distinction is foundational in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) for determining whether qisas (retaliation) or diya (blood money) applies in cases of injury or killing.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Halby who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘The deliberation is all of what something is anticipated, so he hits it with an iron, or with a rock, or with a stick, or with a nudge, so all of these are deliberate; and the error is from anticipating something, so he hits something else’.
